title: Crunchy Granola
subtitle: Honey-oat granola with nuts and seeds
excerpt: Jumbo oats, nuts, and seeds tossed with honey, olive oil, and a little salt, then baked until deeply golden and clumped. Makes a large batch that keeps for two weeks in an airtight jar.

recipe.sourceNotes: Granola was developed in the United States in the late 19th century as a health breakfast. The modern honey-baked version became widespread in the 1960s. Commercial granola is almost universally over-sweetened; home-made granola allows control of the sugar level and results in a better product. The key technique is spreading the granola in a thin, even layer on the baking sheet and leaving it undisturbed during baking so large clumps form.

recipeTools.notes: Two large baking sheets or roasting tins.

content.text: Spread the granola in a single, even layer and do not stir during the first 20 minutes of baking: the clumps form when the honey sets around the oats without disturbance. Leave the granola on the baking sheet to cool completely before breaking into clumps: it crisps as it cools.
Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Line two large baking sheets with baking paper.

Combine the oats, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds in a large bowl. Warm the honey, olive oil, vanilla, and salt together in a small saucepan until the honey has melted and combined with the oil. Pour over the oat mixture and stir until every grain is coated.

Divide between the two baking sheets and spread in a thin, even layer. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, checking after 20 minutes. The granola is ready when it is deeply golden all over. Do not stir during baking.
Remove from the oven. Leave to cool completely on the baking sheets before breaking into clumps. Store in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks.
